threads.body:
The normal LangChain inference path calls `split_system_and_input_messages()` from `on_llm_start`, not this helper; that function's `InputMessage` construction still omits `name`. As a result, named messages continue to lose participant names on inference spans. Please propagate the name in that path as well and cover the callback path in a test.

This issue also appears on line 422 of the same file.
threads.hunk:
@@ -352,10 +352,12 @@ def to_input_messages(
         parts = _message_parts(message)
         if not parts and not _has_content(message):
             continue
+        msg_name = getattr(message, "name", None)
         result.append(
             InputMessage(
                 role=_normalize_role(message) or Role.USER.value,
                 parts=parts,
+                name=str(msg_name) if msg_name is not None else None,

threads.body: The repository's pinned `SEMCONV_GENAI_REF` (`67dff024…`) still requires `finish_reason` and does not allow `null`, while this default permits `OutputMessage(...)` to emit `"finish_reason": null` (as the new test asserts). This diverges from the schema source required by the [util semconv rule](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-python-genai/blob/main/.github/instructions/util-genai.instructions.md#2-semantic-conventions). Please advance the pin and reconcile all affected models/conformance, or keep this field required until the pin advances.
